learningObjective: Diagnose why an autotuner's best-config picks differ across runs and identify the primary contributor.

hardwareContext.architecture: generic sm_80 / sm_90 with default clock governor

profileData:
Run A of autotuner (100 trials): best config = C1 at 0.42 ms; C2 comes second at 0.44 ms.
Run B (same code, same GPU, immediately after Run A): best config = C2 at 0.42 ms; C1 second at 0.45 ms.
Single-config replay: each of C1 and C2 individually measures at 0.42 ± 0.03 ms across 20 replays.
stem: An autotuner picks different 'best' configs across two consecutive runs. Single-config replay shows both configs measure at 0.42 ± 0.03 ms. Which is the most likely root cause and appropriate fix?

options.text: Measurement noise is on the same order as the runtime gap between C1 and C2. Any winner-take-all comparison is dominated by variance; the fix is to increase repetitions per trial and use a robust statistic (e.g., median of medians) or an equivalence band.
The GPU driver has a memory leak; upgrading the driver will fix the non-determinism.
The kernels have a genuine algorithmic difference that only manifests every other launch; C1 and C2 are actually different optima at odd- and even-numbered invocations.
The autotuner is using a broken random seed; setting the seed to a fixed value will make C1 and C2 report identical runtimes.

explanation: When measurement noise (±0.03 ms) is on the same order as the gap between candidates (0.02 ms), a winner-take-all comparison is essentially coin-flipping. This is the canonical problem for autotuners on real hardware: OS scheduling, GPU clock jitter, memory allocator state, and background processes contribute variance. Robust remedies include (a) increasing repetitions per trial, (b) using a statistical band and declaring a tie inside it, and (c) using median/geomean instead of mean. Options B (driver leak) and C (alternating optima) are unsupported. Option D confuses seed determinism with measurement noise — a seed affects the tuner's exploration path, not the underlying kernel runtime.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: standard measurement-noise vs. gap analysis; the fix aligns with Ansor / AutoTVM best practices.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no evidence for a driver leak, and driver leaks would show as monotonic slowdown.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: seeds affect tuner exploration, not kernel runtime.

assumptions: No background workload runs on the same GPU during measurement.
GPU clock governor is default (not locked).
nonImplications: Does not imply autotuning is unusable; robust methodology tames the problem.
Does not imply the gap will always be within noise; sometimes it exceeds noise and the winner is stable.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses seed determinism with kernel-runtime determinism.

performanceClaim.scope: Autotuner winner-take-all variance under real GPU noise
